description: Schema for shadow deployment data collection (commercialization gate G20; see artifacts/release/gap_audit.json). Each record represents one production-like request processed by Veya in shadow mode. Collection switches on VEYA_SHADOW_MODE=1|true (web/server.py _shadow_enabled): responses then carry the X-Veya-Shadow: true header and every telemetry log line (web/server.py _safe_telemetry) carries "shadow": true. Deploy the shadow stack with the kustomize overlay k8s/shadow-overlay (namePrefix shadow-, shadow-mode ConfigMap key forced to "1"). A record joins the telemetry log line, the release hash headers of GET /readyz, the eventual ground-truth label, and the analysis-grade payloads required by the research/veyabench modules.
blocked_reason: Requires production traffic routed to the shadow deployment. No live traffic exists yet (gap_audit.json G20: "Shadow telemetry and drift-monitor tooling are ready and tested, but running a live shadow evaluation requires actual production traffic, which does not exist yet.").

record_schema.description: One record per request. Raw telemetry field names must be preserved verbatim because the research/veyabench analysis modules read them directly (drift_monitor.py reads `timestamp`, `automation`, `ground_truth`, `correct`, `candidate_count`, `route`, `latency_ms`, `confidence`, `config_hash`).

timestamp.description: Telemetry field `timestamp` (web/server.py: datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()). Required by research/veyabench/drift_monitor.py partition_by_time (day/week/month period keys).

request_id.description: Telemetry field `request_id`; echoed back as the X-Request-Id header on error responses.

model_hash.description: SHA-256 of the serving checkpoint. Source: X-Veya-Model-Hash on GET /readyz (web/server.py handle_readyz), taken from the audited model service /version payload `checkpoint_sha256`.

policy_hash.description: SHA-256 of the selective policy artifact held by the serving stack. Source: X-Veya-Policy-Hash on GET /readyz, from /version `selective_policy_sha256`.

config_hash.description: Telemetry field `config_hash` = release manifest SHA-256 (web/server.py: version["release_manifest_sha256"]). drift_monitor.py raises the config_mismatch trigger when a period contains more than one distinct value.

primitive.description: Decision primitive. Enum per web/contracts.py Primitive; production_scope.json refers to the score family as "score-categorical".

prediction.description: Whitelisted model output returned to the caller (web/contracts.py validate_response): decision, answer, probabilities, legend (score), answers (systemone), calibration_version, defer_reason. The eventual ground-truth comparison populates `correct`.

confidence.description: Telemetry field `confidence` in [0, 1], answer-time only; null when the decision is defer. drift_monitor.py skips null confidences when building its histogram.

max_probability.description: Telemetry field `max_probability`: the model's peak output probability in [0, 1]. The gateway captures it server-side from the raw model-service payload before the response whitelist (web/contracts.py validate_response) strips it, so the client-facing HTTP response never carries the score (web/server.py _telemetry_max_probability); the audited bundle serves the field directly (veya/release_bundle.py public_choice) and plain agent responses have it derived from the served distribution. Null on defer, on error paths, and for multi-question systemone requests (no single top-level distribution). Carried verbatim in shadow records alongside `confidence` for selective-risk and drift analysis.

automation.description: Raw telemetry selective decision (web/server.py _safe_telemetry, result.automation). "answer" = accepted/automated; "defer" = not automated; null = decision unavailable (error paths). research/veyabench/drift_monitor.py counts accepted = (automation == "answer"); this exact field name and its values must be preserved.

selective_decision.description: Normalized view of `automation` ("answer" -> "accept"); collected alongside the raw field for reporting. Analysis modules consume `automation`, not this alias.

latency_ms.description: Telemetry field `latency_ms` (integer milliseconds, end-to-end request latency).

ground_truth.description: Eventual ground-truth label; null until labeled. drift_monitor.py computes error_n/risk/risk_ucb95 for a period as soon as any record in it carries ground truth.

correct.description: Whether the prediction matched ground_truth; null until labeled (or when the request errored). drift_monitor.py counts an error when automation == "answer" and `correct` is falsy; selective_gates.py requires it on every case.

slice_metadata.description: Collection-time context; candidate_count and route are telemetry fields.

candidate_count.description: Telemetry field `candidate_count`; feeds the drift_monitor.py candidate-count and input-length distributions.

input_length.description: Observed input length at collection time (not a telemetry field; optional).

language.description: Request language when known; the production scope currently supports en only (production_scope.json).

route.description: Telemetry field `route` (e.g. shortlist_k8_packed_rerank); used as drift_monitor.py's label_distribution fallback and for routing comparisons.

slice_tag.description: Protocol slice condition for robustness gates and drift slices, required by research/veyabench/selective_gates.py and blind_verdict.py case contracts ("clean" is CLEAN_SLICE; KNOWN_SLICE_CONDITIONS also covers the phase11-generic-noise-v1, blind-surface-noise-v1, and blind-template-paraphrase-v1 families).

incumbent_outcome.description: Human/incumbent system decision, null if unavailable. Not consumed by current veyabench modules; collected for incumbent-vs-Veya comparison studies.

sample_size_requirements.description: Minimum sample sizes needed for the statistical release gates, computed by Wilson-interval inversion.
sample_size_requirements.method: research/veyabench/sample_size.py required_n(epsilon, anticipated_coverage, max_errors, confidence=0.95) -> {accepted, total, wilson_ucb_at_accepted}; total = ceil(accepted / anticipated_coverage). Consumed by blind_verdict.py _sample_size_check (protocol Section 7); reference values unit-tested in tests/test_sample_size.py.

parameters.anticipated_coverage: Frozen c_min from the veya-freeze-record-v1 freeze record (research/veyabench/freeze_record.py requires epsilon, c_min, bootstrap_confidence); the drift_monitor.drift_triggers coverage_floor default is 0.05.
parameters.max_errors: Observed accepted-decision error count on the labeled sample (0..3 cover the protocol reference table).

reference_values.note: Required accepted counts are coverage-independent (protocol Section 7 table); totals scale as ceil(accepted / anticipated_coverage) and must be recomputed against the actual c_min.

sample_size_requirements.minimum_labeled_samples: .venv/bin/python -c "from research.veyabench.sample_size import required_n; print(required_n(epsilon=0.02, anticipated_coverage=<c_min>, max_errors=<observed_errors>, confidence=0.95))" — e.g. 189 accepted (957 total at the 0.1977 blind-CLINC150-validation coverage, 593/3000 at threshold 0.02) with zero accepted errors.

acceptance_criteria.note: Every gate below is implemented and fail-closed: a statistic that cannot support its claim fails the gate it feeds (research/veyabench/selective_gates.py). Thresholds marked "frozen" come from the pre-registered veya-freeze-record-v1.

primary_gates.P2_selective_safety: Gate G1_clean_safety — clean-slice risk_ucb95 <= frozen epsilon.
primary_gates.P4_shift_robustness: Gates G2_shift_safety AND G3_coverage_retention AND G4_collapse_floor.
primary_gates.P5_calibration_transfer: Freeze record pins temperature_artifact_sha256; the frozen temperature is applied, never refit on evaluation data.

acceptance_criteria.risk_gate: risk_UCB95 <= epsilon (Wilson upper bound on accepted-decision risk): per-slice via selective_gates.py (G1 clean; G2 every shifted slice) and per-period via drift_monitor.drift_triggers, trigger "risk_breach".
acceptance_criteria.coverage_gate: P3: clean-slice coverage >= frozen c_min; drift_monitor.drift_triggers coverage_floor default 0.05.
acceptance_criteria.retention_gate: G3_coverage_retention: shifted_coverage / clean_coverage >= coverage_retention_min; blind_verdict.py DEFAULT_COVERAGE_RETENTION_MIN = 0.95.
acceptance_criteria.collapse_floor_gate: G4_collapse_floor: no slice below blind_verdict.py DEFAULT_COLLAPSE_FLOOR = {"coverage": 0.05, "accuracy": 0.30}.
acceptance_criteria.calibration_gate: P5_calibration_transfer as above. Per-slice ECE (15 bins, veya.common.ece_score), Brier, reliability diagram, and risk-coverage deciles are reported descriptively by research/veyabench/calibration_report.py; no hard ECE threshold is encoded in code.
acceptance_criteria.drift_gate: No drift_monitor.drift_triggers alert: risk_breach (period risk_ucb95 > epsilon), config_mismatch (more than one config_hash in a period), coverage_drop (period coverage < 0.8 * first-period baseline coverage), distribution_shift (confidence-histogram KS p < 0.01 vs the first period).

analysis_commands.note: research/veyabench analysis modules are library-only (no --data CLI): invoke them from the repository root with the project interpreter, e.g. .venv/bin/python -c "...". <shadow_data.json> is the JSON array of shadow records per record_schema.
analysis_commands.selective_gates: .venv/bin/python -c "import json; from research.veyabench.selective_gates import gate_report; cases = json.load(open('<shadow_data.json>')); policy = json.load(open('artifacts/release/selective_policy.json')); print(json.dumps(gate_report(cases, policy, 0.02, 0.95, {'coverage': 0.05, 'accuracy': 0.30}), indent=2))" — requires a policy whose operating_epsilon enables a threshold: the shipped selective_policy.json has operating_epsilon "disabled" (runtime defers all automation, veya/selective.py apply_threshold semantics), so gate runs need a copy with operating_epsilon set to one of "0.02"/"0.05"/"0.10".
analysis_commands.drift_analysis: .venv/bin/python -c "import json; from research.veyabench.drift_monitor import drift_report, drift_triggers; records = json.load(open('<shadow_data.json>')); report = drift_report(records, period='week'); print(json.dumps(report, indent=2)); print(json.dumps(drift_triggers(report, epsilon=0.02), indent=2))"
analysis_commands.calibration_report: .venv/bin/python -c "import json; from research.veyabench.calibration_report import calibration_report, calibration_summary; payloads = json.load(open('<shadow_calibration_payloads.json>')); print(json.dumps(calibration_summary(calibration_report(payloads, threshold=0.9796500892257723)), indent=2))" — payloads need per-slice logits/labels/confidence/correct/scores under the frozen temperature; the gateway whitelist does not expose logits, so capture them from the audited model service side.
analysis_commands.full_verdict: .venv/bin/python -c "import json; from research.veyabench.blind_verdict import run_blind_verdict, verdict_summary; config = json.load(open('<shadow_verdict_config.json>')); verdict = run_blind_verdict(config); print(json.dumps(verdict, indent=2)); print(verdict_summary(verdict))" — config must carry freeze_record, cases, training_texts, and policy (blind_verdict.py); each case follows the blind case contract (text, gold_label, prediction, correct, probabilities, logits, slice_tag).

report_format.name: veya-shadow-evaluation-v1
report_format.description: The shadow evaluation report is a JSON document whose verdict layer uses the veya-blind-verdict-v1 structure produced by research/veyabench/blind_verdict.py run_blind_verdict (format, freeze_record_hash, contamination, gates, calibration, sample-size check, primary_gates, verdict language), with drift and gate annexes in their own registered formats.
